Agent run

The screen of one agent run inside the app shell: the run's title and its stations at the top, the transcript as a log of messages and step groups, and a dock at the bottom with the jump-to-latest control, the now-doing line and the composer.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • For the screen where a reader watches an agent work, answers its requests and reads its result.
  • For a finished run, with the same header and transcript and the one next action in place of the dock.
  • When you are unsure how the transcript components fit together: which rows are grouped, where approval controls sit, what is announced.

When not to use it

  • For the list of runs. Use a list of run status rows in the app shell.
  • For a queue of approvals from several runs. Use approval cards in a list.
  • For a chat with no tools and no steps. A transcript of messages and a composer is enough: leave the timeline, the groups and the now-doing line out.
  • To show a run's activity as one spinner or one progress bar. The steps are the content.

Accessibility

  • The screen sits in the main column of the app shell. It is a detail screen, so the app header holds a back link to the list of runs and the pending tray, and there is no tab bar. The page header holds the view's one h1, the title of the run.
  • ds-agent-run is the one child of the main column. It holds ds-agent-run__header, with the page header and then the run timeline, then the activity announcer, then ds-agent-run__transcript.
  • The activity announcer is the view's one status region for the run, in the page from the first render. The transcript is a div with ds-agent-run__log, role="log", aria-live="off" and a name, around the ol of rows. Nothing else on the screen announces the run: not the now-doing line, not a time that counts up, not the text that is arriving.
  • What is always in view: the agent's text, a question to the reader, the final answer, and one line for every step or group of steps. One level down, behind a step group's summary: the steps of a finished stretch. Two levels down, behind a step's own summary: its arguments and its output. There is no third level.
  • Three or more consecutive tool calls go in a step group. The app sets open on a group while a step in it runs or awaits approval and when one has failed, and closes a finished group only if the reader has not opened or closed it themselves. The final answer is never inside a group.
  • A step that waits for approval shows Allow and Decline in its row, with secondary emphasis and data-ds-critical. Its group is open and says Awaiting your approval in its summary, and the now-doing line names the wait and links to the row. A wait on the reader takes the now-doing line even while another step runs: that step says Running in its own row and in its group's summary.
  • ds-agent-run__dock is fixed to the bottom of the screen. It holds the jump-to-latest block, the now-doing line and the composer, in that order. Stop is on the now-doing line, so the composer keeps Send, which is the view's one primary action while the run is open. Text sent while the agent works is queued by the app.
  • The transcript follows its newest row only while the reader is at the bottom. In an app without a framework, ds-agent-run__transcript is the ds-transcript element from behaviors/transcript.js and the times are ds-elapsed elements from behaviors/elapsed.js. A framework app uses a div and does both itself.
  • A finished run has no dock. Its groups are closed, its final answer is the last message row, and ds-agent-run__outcome under the log holds the one primary action that moves the work on, with any lesser action beside it at secondary emphasis.
  • While the transcript loads, the header and the timeline are already there and a skeleton with aria-busy stands in for the rows. A run with nothing in it shows a compact empty state under an h2, with suggestion chips, and a timeline whose stations all read Not started.
  • Tab goes through the header, the rows and their summaries in order, then the jump control when it is shown, the link and Stop on the now-doing line, and the composer. Nothing on the screen moves focus by itself.
